doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

title: Facing fear at 84
summary: Griffin says turning 84 left him unafraid, and describes finding, facing and fixing problems and choosing the good side each day.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Did that follow you through your life perhaps with your interpersonal connections with musicians or record labels, club owners?

Yeah, yeah. It did. And then it had, there’s periods where I just had to decide and then I wasn’t using it. Then lately, just maybe a year or a few months, I got back to it. Because I just turned 84 on January 28. Then I said, you know ain’t nothing, I’m not afraid of anything now. I’m not even afraid of death. Because death is inevitable. It’s going to happen. So I say why don’t you face your fears. There’s a saying that says the three F’s. Find it, face it, and fix it. And the thing that keeps you from finding it and facing it and fixing it is fear. That’s the fourth F. So I say now most of the time we find the problem, we even face it but we don’t fix it because we fear the results. So I am less fearful, you know, of anything than I have been all my life, and just turned 84. So it’s just, and then I wake up and I like am more excited. I pick up the horn and I play it differently. I just — this whole thing about the head and the tails of any coin — and that’s the way life is. Everything you have, everything you have is good. There’s a bad waiting on the other side. A balance. And you know you’ve got to figure out where you’re going to be on a particular side of anything. Are you going to be on the left side or the right side? Good side or the bad side? The light side or the dark side? The happy side or the sad side. And you make those choices every day.
I can tell I’m going to feel better after talking to you today.

Oh thank you. Because you make those choices. You know like a lot of times you wake up, you’re feeling bad and everything, but are you going to let that bad feeling prevail throughout your day? No. You go to the good feeling.
